title: Majestic Knishop
summary: Use a knight check to win the queen after the bishop’s diversion.

nodes.question: Where can the knight check and attack the queen?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Qxd7, with White Kc3/Nc4/b4/c5 against Ka4/Qd7/e5. The earlier nine-piece knight checks and bishop sacrifice are source context; this exact seven-piece finish is reconstructed separately.

branches.title: Fork and collect the diverted queen
commentary: Begin after Black’s queen has accepted the bishop sacrifice on d7. Only this supported later phase is checked here.
Nb6+ checks Ka4 and attacks Qd7. The bishop’s earlier diversion has put the queen on a knight-fork square.
Ka3 is the illustrated king escape. Black’s king must answer the check before its queen can move.
Nxd7 wins the queen. White retains a checked win with knight and connected pawns; this is not immediate mate.
branches.explanation: Nxd7 wins the queen. White retains a checked win with knight and connected pawns; this is not immediate mate.

branches.title: Compare another king escape from the fork
commentary: Compare an independently supplied legal king reply to the same fork.
Nb6+ attacks king and queen simultaneously.
Kb5 escapes the knight check but still leaves Qd7 attacked.
Nxd7 wins the queen. This exact knight-and-pawn ending is winning, though further conversion is not encoded.

exercises.prompt: What makes the bishop sacrifice useful to the final knight?
exercises.answer: It draws the queen to d7. From c4, Nb6+ then checks the king and attacks that queen in one move.
